chunks: Those who fear God and follow the straight path will surely be in gardens and in bliss,

key_terms.الْمُتَّقِينَ: The God-fearing; those who possess taqwa (God-consciousness)
key_terms.جَنَّاتٍ: Gardens; a common term for Paradise (Jannah) in the Quran
key_terms.نَعِيمٍ: Bliss; eternal pleasure and comfort in the afterlife

ai.seo_question: What is the ultimate reward for those who are God-fearing (al-muttaqin)?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah Al-Waqi'ah (or Al-Ma'arij depending on specific recitation context, though often cited in eschatological discussions) underscores the dual nature of Paradise as both a physical abode (Jannat) and a state of profound spiritual contentment (Na'im). The term 'al-muttaqin' is interpreted not merely as the pious but as those who possess 'taqwa'—a conscious guarding against spiritual negligence through adherence to the Ahl al-Bayt's teachings. This reward signifies the culmination of the soul's journey from the material world to the divine presence, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the unity of inner faith and outer action.
